eligibility_reason: A discovery GWAS of SLE (new GWAS + meta-analysis with the existing Hom et al. 2008 data + a 'replication study' cohort). The replication cohort validates SNPs selected from this paper's own GWAS/meta-analysis (a within-paper, statistical-sense replication stage), and the Hom et al. component reanalyses existing data; no prior published finding is framed or tested as a replication target.
why_negative: Within-paper GWAS replication stage ('replicates' in the statistical sense) plus reanalysis of an existing GWAS dataset; the paper is a locus-discovery study, not a replication of specific published findings.
notes: The 'replication study' (2,018 new cases, 6,925 controls; Online Methods 'Data: replication study') genotypes the 33 SNPs that passed thresholds in the meta-analysis of this paper's GWAS and Hom et al. (Supplementary Table 2); its purpose is to confirm this paper's own candidate signals, so it is a within-paper replication. Hom et al. (2008) data are re-analysed, not newly collected. A second coder might argue for positive entries because many of the 43 loci were previously published (e.g. 'Five other genes (TNIP1, IKZF1, ETS1, WDFY4 and ARID5B) that we mapped are novel in European SLE, but had been previously shown to be associated with SLE in Chinese subjects5,6' = Han et al. 2009 Nat Genet; Yang et al. 2010 PLoS Genet), which would read as close-extension successes in a European population. I did not code these because the paper does not present them as replications of those studies, the GWAS discovery data are not 'new data collected to test' those claims, and per-locus entries would be dozens of rows with no authorial replication framing. Note also that the heritability comparison with So et al. (2011) is a computation, not a replication. The text rendition of Table 1 was read; the PDF was not needed.
